title: Sorting press: Total receipt
topics: Recursion, sorting, binary search and bits
summary: Produce readings sorted numerically ascending using a merge-based divide-and-conquer approach. Keep duplicate readings. Return the sum of all values in the derived sequence; return 0 for an empty sequence.
descriptionMd:
Two small sorted proof trays are repeatedly joined by the office's divide-and-merge press. Pia is closing the print-room account before the afternoon mail. A single total must replace the pile of working slips.

Produce readings sorted numerically ascending using a merge-based divide-and-conquer approach. Keep duplicate readings.

Return the sum of all values in the derived sequence; return 0 for an empty sequence.

Implement sortingPressTotalReceipt(readings, k). k is part of the common inspection-card signature and does not affect this task's result.
unitIntro: Merge sort. Produce readings sorted numerically ascending using a merge-based divide-and-conquer approach. Keep duplicate readings. Keep the sequence order specified here before computing the requested receipt. A scan invariant says what has been processed and what remains. Work through the proof strip first, then change the returned summary without changing the definition of that sequence. The last card revisits loop accumulators from Hello, Keys.
constraints: 1 <= k <= 8. All arithmetic results fit a signed 32-bit integer.
Numeric readings lie between -1,000,000 and 1,000,000, subject to the task's shape and ordering rules.

Target time O(n log n); auxiliary space including the derived sequence O(n). n is the input length; d distinct values; q query count; M maximum reading; V vertices; E edges; h tree height; r reported tree nodes.
hints: Start with merge sort. What state describes the portion you have already processed?

Produce readings sorted numerically ascending using a merge-based divide-and-conquer approach. Keep duplicate readings. Derive each required reading once; do not restart the whole procedure for every output position.
Return the sum of all values in the derived sequence; return 0 for an empty sequence. Handle the empty derived sequence according to the stated return rule.

cases.explanation: The derived sequence is [-3,0,7,7,12]. Return the sum of all values in the derived sequence; return 0 for an empty sequence. This gives 23.
The derived sequence is [-2,4,4,4]. Return the sum of all values in the derived sequence; return 0 for an empty sequence. This gives 10.
The derived sequence is []. Return the sum of all values in the derived sequence; return 0 for an empty sequence. This gives 0.

overview: Variation: Merge sort. Build the sequence once, then report exactly what the inspection card requests.
